intervals.text: THE SVMME AND PARTITION OF THE HOLIE BIBLE.
With a brife note of the Canonical and Apochryphal Bookes.

BY the vniforme conſent of al learned Diuines, the holie Bible, or vvritten vvord of God, conteyneth expreſſed or implied, al thinges that man is to beleue, to obſerue, & to auoid, for obtayning of eternal ſaluation. That is , al matters of faith & maners, by vvhich vve may knovv and ſerue God, and ſo be ſpiritually ioyned vvith him, in this life, & in eternitie. For both the old & nevv Teſtament propoſe and teſtifie vnto vs, one and the ſame God, the ſame Chriſt, the ſame Church, and other Myſteries of our beleefe, not differing in ſubſtance, but in maner of vttering ; the Old more obſcurely in figures and prophecies foretelling thoſe thinges, vvhich the New declareth (in great part) as donne and performed. VVherupon ſaith S. Auguſtin : In the Old Teſtament the New lieth hidden : & in the New the Old lieth open. And touching their names ; vvherein appareth difference, the one (ſaith the ſame Doctor) is called the old Teſtament , either becauſe it propoſeth promiſes of temporal thinges (VVhervvith our old corruptnes is allured) Or in reſpect of the New, by which it is fulfilled , and in ſome part aboliſhed. The other is called the New, becauſe by it man is renewed, and hath promiſe of eternal life : VVhich ſhal neuer vvaxe old nor decay. Likevviſe S. Gregorie the great teſtifieth this conformitie, and correſpondence betvven the Old and New Teſtament, affirming that the ſame is ſignified by the Prophet Ezechiels viſion of a vvheele, vvhich had foure faces, or apparence of foure vvhiles, the ſhape vvhereof vvas, as it vvete, a wheele in the middes of a wheele. What is this ſaith he, niſi quod in Teſtamenti veteris litera Teſtamentum nouum latuit per Allegoriam ? but that in the letter of the old Teſtament, the New lay hidden by an Allegorie ?

And as the ſame is the ſumme and ſubiect of both Teſtaments : ſo both are diuided (for the more principal partes therof) into foure ſortes of Bookes: Legal, Hiſtorical, Sapiential, & Prophetical. The Legal bookes of the old Teſtament are the fiue Bookes of Moiſes ; Geneſis, Exodus, Leuiticus, Numeri, & Deuteronomie ; vvhereto anſvver in the nevv Teſtament, the foure Goſpels of S. Matthew, S. Marke, S. Luke, & S. Iohn. Hiſtorical bookes of the old Teſtament, are the Bookes of Ioſue, Iudges, Ruth, foure bookes of Kinges, two of Paralipomenon, Eſdras vvith Nehemias, Tobias, Iudith, Heſter, Iob, & two of the Machabees ; vnto vvhich, in the nevv Teſtament, anſvver the Actes of the Apoſtles. Sapiential, of the old Teſtament, are the Prouerbes, Eccleſiaſtes, Canticles, Booke of wiſdome, & Eccleſiaſticus ; and of like ſorte are in the nevv Teſtament, the Epiſtles of S. Paul & of other Apoſtles. Prophetical bookes are Dauids Pſalter (vvhich is alſo Sapiential, yea likevviſe Legal and Hiſtorical) the Bookes of Iſaias, Ieremias vvith Baruch, Ezechiel, Daniel, the tvvelue leſſe Prophetes, Oſea, Ioel, Amos, Abdias, Ionas, Michæas, Nahum, Abacuc, Sophonias, Aggæus, Zacharias, Malachias . And in the nevv Teſtament, the Apocalips of S. Iohn the Apoſtle.

Al theſe Bookes are vndoubtedly Canonical, as the Authores cited in the inner margent teſtifie . And conſequently al, and al the partes therof ; are of infallible truth. For othervviſe as S. Auguſtin teacheth, if anie part vvere falſe, or doubtful , al vvere vncertaine. once admittiug falſehood (ſaith he, Epiſt. 8. ad Ieroni) in ſuch ſoueraigne authoritie, no parcel of theſe bookes should remaine, which anie way should ſeme hard to maners, or incredible to beleue, but it might by this moſt pernicious rule be turned to an officious fiction of the author. That is : If anie error could be committed by the authores of Scriptures, either through ignorance, obliuion, or anie other humane frailtie, vvhatſoeuer vvere produced, exception might be taken, and queſtion made, vvhether the author had erred, or no ? True it is, that ſome of theſe bookes (as we ſhal particularly diſcuſſe in their places) vvere ſometimes doubted of by ſome Catholiques, and called Apochrypal, in that ſenſe, as the vvord properly ſignifieth hidden, or not apparent. So S. Ierom (in his Prologue before the Latin Bible) calleth diuers bookes Apochryphal, being not ſo euident, VVhether they vvere Diuine ſcripture, becauſe they vvere not in the Ievves Canon, nor at firſt in the Churches Canon, but vvere neuer reiected, as falſe or erronious. In vvhich ſenſe the Prayer of Manaſſes, the third booke-of-Eſdras, and third of Machabees are yet called Apochryphal. As for the fourth of Eſdras, and fourth of Machabees there is more doubt. But diuers others, as the booke aſcribed to Enoch, the Goſpels of S. Andrew, S. Thomas, S. Bartholmew, and the like recited by ſ. Gelaſius (Decreto de libris Eccleſiaſticis diſt. 15. Can. Sancta Romana) S. Innocentius the firſt (Epiſt. 3.) S. Ierom, Ep. ad Latam, S. Auguſtin li. 15. cap. 23. de ciuit. Dei. Origen homiſ. 2. in Cantica. are in a vvorſe ſenſe called Apochryphal, & are reiected as
